newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to up despite softer crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to up despite softer crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were steady to up slightly Friday in lackluster trade, but further weakness in crude, soft gas prices and mild weather forecasts for later next week should limit any upside, sources said.

"There's no big demand, and as far as price is concerned, resid isn't even in the running (against gas)," said one East Coast utility source, adding he expected more selling ahead as winter drew to a close.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent edged up 25 cents to the $16.50-75 a barrel level on reports of a cargo sale late Thursday at $17.35 (delivered Mass.), traders said.
NYH March one percent paper eased slightly with softer crude to the low-$16 area.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally gained a quarter to $17.50, but mild weather later next week and soft city gate gas prices should keep buyers relaxed.
New York city gate gas prices again eased slightly to the $2.12/mmBtu area, or about a $13.35 a barrel equivalent.
NYH high sulphurs also were steady to up modestly, with three percent now at about $15.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices again were stable, with one percent still at $15.25 and three percent at $13.00-25.
